arxiv-2011-09378.title: LAVA: Latent Action Spaces via Variational Auto-encoding for Dialogue Policy Optimization
arxiv-2011-09378.creator: Nurul Lubis, Christian Geishauser, Michael Heck, Hsien-chin Lin
arxiv-2011-09378.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning (RL) can enable task-oriented dialogue systems to steer the conversation towards successful task completion. In an end-to-end setting, a response can be constructed in a word-level sequential decision making process with the entire system vocabulary as action space.

arxiv-2209-01159.title: Recursive greedy initialization of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm with guaranteed improvement
arxiv-2209-01159.creator: Stefan H. Sack, Raimel A. Medina, Richard Kueng, Maksym Serbyn
arxiv-2209-01159.description: Abstract The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a variational quantum algorithm, where a quantum computer implements a variational ansatz consisting of p p layers of alternating unitary operators and a classical computer is used to optimize the variational parameters.

arxiv-2211-15658.title: Connecting the Dots: Floorplan Reconstruction Using Two-Level Queries
arxiv-2211-15658.creator: Yuanwen Yue, Theodora Kontogianni, Konrad Schindler, Francis Engelmann
arxiv-2211-15658.description: Abstract We address 2D floorplan reconstruction from 3D scans. Existing approaches typically employ heuristically designed multi-stage pipelines. Instead, we formulate floorplan reconstruction as a single-stage structured prediction task: find a variable-size set of polygons, which in turn are variable-length sequences of ordered vertices.

arxiv-2304-07799.description: Abstract In inertial confinement fusion (ICF) implosions, mixing the ablator into the fuel and the hot spot is one of the most adverse factors that lead to ignition degradation. arxiv-2402-15564.title: Interplay of superexchange and vibronic effects in the hidden order of Ba 2 MgReO 6 from first principles
arxiv-2402-15564.creator: Dario Fiore Mosca, Cesare Franchini, Leonid V. Pourovskii
arxiv-2402-15564.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dario Fiore Mosca, Cesare Franchini, Leonid V. Pourovskii. The origin of the ”hidden” quadrupolar and unconventional magnetic low-temperature orders observed in the spin-orbit double perovskite Ba 2 MgReO 6 defies explanation through standard experimental and theoretical techniques. Here we address this problem by deriving and solving an ab initio low-temperature effective Hamiltonian including inter-site electronic exchange and vibronic (electron-lattice) couplings between J eff = 3 / 2 J_{\mathrm{eff}}=3/2 Jahn-Teller-active Rhenium states.

arxiv-2601-20125.title: Membership Inference Attacks Against Fine-tuned Diffusion Language Models
arxiv-2601-20125.creator: Yuetian Chen, Kaiyuan Zhang, Yuntao Du, Edoardo Stoppa, Charles Fleming, Ashish Kundu, Bruno Ribeiro, & Ninghui Li
arxiv-2601-20125.description: Abstract Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) represent a promising alternative to autoregressive language models, using bidirectional masked token prediction. Yet their susceptibility to privacy leakage via Membership Inference Attacks (MIA) remains critically underexplored. This paper presents the first systematic investigation of MIA vulnerabilities in DLMs. Unlike the autoregressive models’ single fixed prediction pattern, DLMs’ multiple maskable configurations exponentially increase attack opportunities.

pmc-10480223.title: Complexity measure based on sensitivity analysis applied to an intensive care unit system
pmc-10480223.creator: Joao R. B. Paiva, Viviane M. G. Pacheco, Poliana S. Barbosa, Fabiana R. Almeida, Gabriel A. Wainer, Flavio A. Gomes, Antonio P. Coimbra, Wesley P. Calixto
pmc-10480223.description: This work proposes a system complexity metric and its application to Intensive Care Unit (ICU) system. The methodology for applying said complexity metric comprises: (i) parameters sensitivity indices calculation, (ii) mapping connections dynamics between system components, and (iii) system’s complexity calculation.

pmc-10514391.title: Interest of preoperative embolization of aneurysmal bone cyst (ABC): A case report
pmc-10514391.creator: Moustapha Diallo, Abdoulaye Dione Diop, Ibrahima Niang, Mbaye Thiam, Fallou Gallass Niang, Aminata Diack, Mame Diarra Bousso Ndaw, Ndeye Isseu Amar, Ababacar Mbengue, Abdoulaye Ndoye Diop
pmc-10514391.description: Aneurysmal bone cyst (ABC) is a rare lesion that primarily affects young adults and children. The optimal treatment approach for ABC remains controversial and varies depending on the preferences of the medical team. While some advocate for surgery as the treatment of choice, others recommend a less invasive first-line option such as selective embolization.

pmc-10600250.title: Climate change projected to impact structural hillslope connectivity at the global scale
pmc-10600250.creator: Alexander T. Michalek, Gabriele Villarini, Admin Husic
pmc-10600250.description: Structural connectivity describes how landscapes facilitate the transfer of matter and plays a critical role in the flux of water, solutes, and sediment across the Earth’s surface. The strength of a landscape’s connectivity is a function of climatic and tectonic processes, but the importance of these drivers is poorly understood, particularly in the context of climate change.

pmc-10615388.title: Neuralgic amyotrophy: sensitivity and specificity of magnetic resonance neurography in diagnosis: A retrospective study
pmc-10615388.creator: Luyao Duan, Liyang Zhao, Ying Liu, Yizhe Zhang, Wensong Zheng, Xiaoman Yu, Hongran Liu, Zequn Li, Zhigang Peng, Xiaona Li
pmc-10615388.description: Background:Neuralgic amyotrophy (NA) is a clinically acute or subacute disease. To study the characteristics of brachial plexus magnetic resonance neurography (MRN) in patients with NA, and to explore the clinical application value of MRN combined with electromyography (EMG) in the diagnosis of NA.Methods:Brachial plexus MRN images of 32 patients with NA were retrospectively analyzed, and their characteristics were investigated.

pmc-11389790.title: Modeling Lewy body disease with SNCA triplication iPSC-derived cortical organoids and identifying therapeutic drugs
pmc-11389790.creator: Yunjung Jin, Fuyao Li, Zonghua Li, Tadafumi C. Ikezu, Justin O’Leary, Manikandan Selvaraj, Yiyang Zhu, Yuka A. Martens, Shunsuke Koga, Hannah Santhakumar, Yonghe Li, Wenyan Lu, Yang You, Kiara Lolo, Michael DeTure, Alexandra I. Beasley, Mary D. Davis, Pamela J. McLean, Owen A. Ross, Takahisa Kanekiy
pmc-11389790.description: Aggregated α-synuclein (α-SYN) proteins, encoded by the SNCA gene, are hallmarks of Lewy body disease (LBD), affecting multiple brain regions. However, the specific mechanisms underlying α-SYN pathology in cortical neurons, crucial for LBD-associated dementia, remain unclear. Here, we recapitulated α-SYN pathologies in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs)–derived cortical organoids generated from patients with LBD with SNCA gene triplication.

pmc-11455057.title: 5149 In-vitro Combo Treatment of Human Liver Cancer cell (Hep-G2) Line with Vitamin-A and RU-486
pmc-11455057.creator: Pandurangan Ramaraj
pmc-11455057.description: Disclosure: P. Ramaraj: None.Our previous in-vitro studies involving vitamins (vitamin-A and vitamin-D3) and steroids (progesterone and RU-486) pointed to a combination of vitamin-A and RU-486 as an efficient combo to decrease human melanoma cell growth. We extended this combo treatment to human liver cancer cell (Hep-G2) line.

pmc-11599753.title: Modeling of Bayesian machine learning with sparrow search algorithm for cyberattack detection in IIoT environment
pmc-11599753.creator: Faten Khalid Karim, José Varela-Aldás, Mohamad Khairi Ishak, Ayman Aljarbouh, Samih M. Mostafa
pmc-11599753.description: With the fast-growing interconnection of smart technologies, the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has revolutionized how industries work by connecting devices and sensors and automating regular operations via the Internet of Things (IoTs). IoT devices provide seamless diversity and connectivity in different application domains. This system and its transmission channels are subjected to targeted cyberattacks due to their round-the-clock connectivity.

pmc-11610243.title: Students’ motivation and engagement in interprofessional education: the mediating role of peer relatedness
pmc-11610243.creator: Fraide A Ganotice Jr, Norman B Mendoza, John Ian Wilzon T Dizon, Xiaoai Shen, Jetty Chung-Yung Lee, Enoch Chan, Pauline Luk, Michael M Manio, Qing He, Ui Soon Khoo, May P S Lam, So Ching Sarah Chan, Amy Yin Man Chow, Ning Wang, George L Tipoe
pmc-11610243.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionStudents’ peer relatedness is vital to their academic achievement and engagement. However, little is known about the mechanisms that can explain such a link in health professions education, especially in interprofessional education (IPE), where interprofessional socialization is promoted.

pmc-11626462.title: Development and validation of a French job-exposure matrix for healthcare workers: JEM Soignances
pmc-11626462.creator: Allison Singier, Marc Fadel, Fabien Gilbert, Soignances group, Ester-MESuRS collaboration on occupational risks, Laura Temime, Marie Zins, Alexis Descatha
pmc-11626462.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to develop and evaluate a job-exposure matrix (JEM) specific to healthcare workers, JEM Soignances, based on self-reported data.MethodsThe JEM was constructed using data from healthcare workers within the CONSTANCES cohort (N=12 489). Job titles and sectors of activity (eg, hospital activities) defined occupational groups. We assessed 24 exposures covering organizational, psychosocial, physical, chemical and biological factors.

pmc-12586844.title: Osteoporosis: molecular pathogenesis and therapeutic interventions
pmc-12586844.creator: Xubin Zhang, Yongsheng Liang, Fayao Zhang, Xiaoyuan Liu
pmc-12586844.description: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disease. Genetic and environmental factors work together to cause increased bone resorption, decreased bone formation, bone remodeling imbalance, reduced bone mass, and increased bone fragility. The global incidence of osteoporosis is relatively high, and osteoporosis negatively affects health and quality of life.

pmc-12595134.title: Recent highlights from the International Journal of Cardiology: Heart & Vasculature: Valvular heart disease
pmc-12595134.creator: Francesco Pelliccia, Artur Dziewierz, Marco Zimarino, Dobromir Dobrev
pmc-12595134.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). f life and increase life expectancy. In most patients, the diagnosis of significant VHD can be made based on a physical examination, yet nearly half of the patients who could benefit from intervention are not being recognized or referred. There have been major improvements in both the diagnosis and treatment of patients with VHD, with noninvasive echocardiography available to confirm the presence and severity of VHD, better and more durable surgical procedures, and the advent of catheter-based therapies.

pmc-13007694.title: Do You See the Difference Between Perfection and Excellence?
pmc-13007694.creator: Marilyn Chreim, Thomas Boivin, Denis Cousineau
pmc-13007694.description: PurposeThis research investigated factors affecting statistics anxiety in university students to find out whether perfectionists are at greater risk of experiencing it. This topic is known to be amongst the most anxiety-provoking matter among undergraduate students in the social sciences, humanities, and psychology.

pmc-13276616.title: An integrated multiscale imaging workflow to resolve intracellular co-pathology in human FFPE brain tissue

pmc-13315605.title: Pre-clinical efficacy of a candidate outer membrane vesicle gonococcal vaccine in comparison with 4CMenB
pmc-13315605.creator: Paula Freixeiro, Lisa A. Lewis, Leonor Sánchez-Busó, Magnus Unemo, Sunita Gulati, Aline Linder, Jukka Corander, Odile B. Harrison, Christina Dold, Simon Harris, Christine S. Rollier, Sanjay Ram, Calman A. MacLennan
pmc-13315605.description: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes 82 million global cases of gonorrhoea annually. Multidrug-resistant gonococci threaten to make gonorrhoea untreatable. Meningococcal vaccines MeNZB and 4CMenB (Bexsero), containing Neisseria meningitidis group B detergent-extracted outer membrane vesicles (dOMV), cross-protect against gonorrhoea with 31–59% effectiveness. We hypothesised that gonococcal OMV-based vaccines would have greater efficacy against gonorrhoea than meningococcal vaccines.

pmc-13414218.title: Beyond the platform: why surgical quality and surgeon proficiency outweigh the RATS vs. VATS debate in early-stage lung cancer
pmc-13414218.creator: Marcello Migliore, Kwon Joong Na
pmc-13414218.description: The debate regarding the oncological superiority of Robotic-Assisted Thoracic Surgery (RATS) versus Video-Assisted Thoracic Surgery (VATS) for early-stage lung cancer is ongoing. Current evidence suggests comparable oncological outcomes between the two approaches. This perspective posits that long-term survival relies less on the platform itself and more on the “surgeon factor”—specifically, the tenacity for radical lymph node dissection.

pmc-13593964.title: Don’t forget the world outside the lab – a comment on “Illusions of Understanding in the Sciences”
pmc-13593964.creator: Dominik Bachmann, Leendert van Maanen, Gijs A Holleman, Christian P Janssen
pmc-13593964.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The article “Illusions of Understanding in the Sciences” by Shiffrin et al. (2026) describes ways in which scientists can mislead themselves and others about the extent to which they understand the (causal underpinnings of) phenomena they research. In this reply, we highlight how such “illusions of understanding” can arise from researchers overestimating the extent to which their results generalize beyond curated lab conditions.

pmc-7618488.title: Dopaminergic computations for perceptual decisions
pmc-7618488.creator: Samuel Liebana, Matthias Fritsche, Armin Lak
pmc-7618488.description: Studies linking the brain’s dopamine signals with learning and decision making have enjoyed enormous progress using predominantly value-based decision-making tasks. However, recent studies have demonstrated pervasive dopamine signaling also during perceptual decision making. These signals have been shown to depend on both feedback and perceptual parameters such as perceptual decision confidence and sensory statistics.
